title: Read-back or hear-back
excerpt: Air traffic control clearances are read back by the pilot and checked by the controller, catching misheard altitudes and headings before they matter.

title: Summary of the Amazon S3 Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
excerpt: A mistyped maintenance command removed more servers than intended; the tool was changed to remove capacity slowly and refuse to go below a safe minimum.

title: A Surgical Safety Checklist to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality in a Global Population
cite: Haynes et al., New England Journal of Medicine, 2009
excerpt: Introducing the WHO surgical safety checklist in eight hospitals around the world cut deaths and complications after surgery.

title: Interaction ruling animal collective behavior depends on topological rather than metric distance
excerpt: Each starling in a flock tracks a fixed number of nearest neighbours, about six or seven, which keeps the flock cohesive without a leader.

title: The Box: How the Shipping Container Made the World Smaller and the World Economy Bigger
excerpt: A standard box with standard corner fittings let ports, ships, trucks and railways organize independently and cut the cost of moving goods worldwide.

title: PEP 13: Python Language Governance
excerpt: After its creator stepped down as benevolent dictator for life, Python moved to an elected steering council with fixed terms.

title: Transfer of power
excerpt: The creator of Python steps down as benevolent dictator for life and asks the core developers to decide their own governance.

title: The Checklist
excerpt: After the 1935 crash of Boeing's Model 299, test pilots created a written checklist; checklists later spread to intensive care and cut infections.

title: Y2K Aftermath: Crisis Averted
cite: U.S. Senate Special Committee on the Year 2000 Technology Problem, 2000
excerpt: Years of remediation of the year 2000 date problem meant the feared failures did not happen: a non-event produced by work.

title: Consent Order: Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.
excerpt: Under sales goals, employees opened deposit and credit card accounts customers did not request: a gamed target.

title: Mumbai's Models of Service Excellence
excerpt: Mumbai's dabbawalas deliver around 200,000 home-cooked lunches a day using a painted code on each box and a relay of couriers, without computers.

title: The History of the Bar Code
excerpt: The Universal Product Code was first scanned in 1974 on a pack of chewing gum; one small shared standard reorganized retail and supply chains.

title: UPC: The transformation of retail
excerpt: How the grocery industry agreed on a single product code and symbol, and how scanning changed checkout and inventory.

title: Ancient Double-Entry Bookkeeping: Lucas Pacioli's Treatise
excerpt: The first printed description of double-entry bookkeeping: every transaction recorded twice, so the books check themselves.

title: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
excerpt: A treaty ratified by every country that phased out ozone-depleting substances, with adjustments that tighten schedules without a new treaty.

title: About the Universal Postal Union
excerpt: Postal services of nearly every country agree on rules that let a letter posted anywhere reach any address, with no single carrier in charge.

title: Root KSK Ceremonies
excerpt: A scripted, recorded ceremony with witnesses and split keys that signs the key securing the internet's domain name system.

title: Architectural Principles of the Internet (RFC 1958)
excerpt: The internet's few architectural principles: connectivity is its own reward, end-to-end, and a minimal shared core.

title: Summary of Principles Agreed at the First International Strategy Meeting on Human Genome Sequencing (Bermuda Principles)
excerpt: Sequencing centres agreed to release sequence data publicly within 24 hours, coordinating a global project through a shared rule.

title: A guide to the Kernel Development Process
excerpt: Thousands of developers coordinate through a time-based release cycle, a merge window, a hierarchy of maintainers and patches by email.

title: Kidney Exchange
cite: Roth, Sönmez & Ünver, Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2004
excerpt: A designed clearinghouse lets incompatible patient-donor pairs swap donors in cycles and chains, increasing transplants.

title: An Investigation of the Therac-25 Accidents
excerpt: A radiation therapy machine overdosed patients after hardware interlocks were replaced by software checks with race conditions.

title: External Technical Root Cause Analysis: Channel File 291
excerpt: A content update pushed to every machine at once crashed millions of Windows computers; staged rollout followed.

title: In the Matter of Knight Capital Americas LLC (SEC order)
excerpt: Old trading code reactivated on one server sent millions of orders in 45 minutes, with no automated check to stop them.

title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
excerpt: Models found ways to communicate by writing files into a package manager, turning it into an unintended message board for agents.

title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
excerpt: A state-sponsored group used an AI coding agent to run most steps of an espionage campaign against about thirty targets.

title: California water rate data: strategy report
excerpt: Making one thing hard, a published address for each utility's current rate schedule, so rates can be found and compared.

title: Seven precedents for water rate discovery
excerpt: Precedents for making public data discoverable through a published address and registry.

title: Five cases in data coordination
excerpt: Five cases of coordinating public data across many independent publishers.
